_meta.description: Tactical 24h schedule the Phase-2 office simulation reads each simulated work day. agent-runner.js's runWorkDayCycle() iterates `blocks` in order within a single invocation (no per-block cron yet — see 'cron_status'). Each block represents a point in the simulated day where a specific activity fires, so the day's ~50-case CRM pool, meetings, AI-experience reports, and spare time are spread out instead of all happening at once.
_meta.cron_status: LIVE (re-enabled 2026-07-18 for the Q&A engine's first activation, after the 2026-07-08 pause). OFFICE HOURS since 2026-08-06: wrangler.toml carries TWO Cloudflare Cron Triggers ('*/30 5-14 * * *' and '0 15 * * *') = every 30 min from 05:00 to 15:00 UTC = 08:00-18:00 IDT inclusive, 21 ticks/day. The second expression exists solely to catch the 18:00 boundary tick without also firing at 18:30, which a single '*/30 5-15' would. This REPLACES the 2026-07-18 window ('*/30 0-13,23 * * *' = 02:00-16:30 Israel, 30 ticks/day), which was set to the owner's own activity window rather than to office hours; all case_batch blocks that sat before 08:00 were retimed into the window in the same change — see _office_hours_retime_2026_08_06 below. Each tick, agent-runner.js's scheduled() converts event.scheduledTime to Israel local time (israelTimeParts()) and calls runScheduledBlock(env, time, dayOfWeek), which is a no-op unless a block below has that exact `time` for that day-of-week (note: the 02:00-Israel blocks therefore fire at 23:00 UTC the PREVIOUS calendar day — israelTimeParts() handles the day-of-week rollover). Day-in-progress state lives in SIM_KV under 'daily-cycle-state' between blocks. Per-block errors (e.g. Gemini 429) are logged to `reports` (logScheduledError) and do not abort the day.

week_mapping.description: dayOfWeek = ((current_day - 1) % 7) + 1, as already computed by runWorkDayCycle(). This schedule maps it to an Israeli Sun-Thu work week per the Launch Decisions ('work days Sunday-Thursday'), with Friday as a short summary day and Saturday off.
week_mapping.6: Friday (short day — weekly summary meeting, reduced case load)
week_mapping.7: Saturday (REST DAY, and since 2026-08-10 a genuinely zero-write one — no case batches, no meetings, no model calls, no repo commit. The previous text here said Saturday was 'NOT a zero-API-calls day' because of the Guides verification pass; that pass moved to Friday 11:30 and the day-finalize commit is now suppressed on off days. See saturday_schedule._rest_day_2026_08_10 and docs/OFFICE-POLICY.md A13 in back-office.)

_meta.case_volume_design_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-18 (Q&A-engine rebuild) — volume is no longer a fixed per-agent quota at all. Once per day, at cycle start, agent-runner.js's computeDailyQuestionVolume() checks the remaining shared Claude budget for the month (config/token-economy.json shared_claude_budget) and picks a conservative day total from it (0 if exhausted) — never a fixed number decided in advance. That total is then SPREAD across the day exactly as before, via the existing case_batch case_share proportions below (6 case_batch blocks, 08:00-15:00 Israel since the 2026-08-06 office-hours retime — was 02:00-15:00 — roughly 90 minutes apart; full_day_schedule has 11 blocks total — the 6 case batches plus tool_task_window, chore_rotation, report, standup meeting, and spare_time). Non-burstiness for Notebook-X specifically doesn't come from this per-day total at all — it comes from workers/gemini-pacer.js's per-call pacing check at ask time (agent-base.js askAssignedProject()), which is what actually rate-limits Gemini calls regardless of how many questions a block was handed.

_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.what: All case_batch blocks that sat before 08:00 Israel were moved into the 08:00-18:00 office-hours window, in the same change that narrowed the Cloudflare cron to that window (wrangler.toml: '*/30 5-14 * * *' + '0 15 * * *' = 08:00-18:00 IDT).
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.why: This file already declared work_hours.start = 08:00 while scheduling case batches at 02:00, 04:30 and 07:00 — hours before its own stated start. The blocks never matched the declaration. Narrowing the cron did not break the schedule's intent; it exposed a contradiction the file had been carrying. Owner decision 2026-08-06: retime the blocks to agree with the declaration rather than widen the cron back out.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.volume_is_UNCHANGED_and_that_is_the_poin: NO case_share VALUE WAS EDITED. The block COUNT per schedule is unchanged (6 Sun-Thu, 3 Friday) and each block kept its original share, in its original order — only `time` moved. Sun-Thu still sums to 1.00 (0.20/0.15/0.15/0.15/0.15/0.20) and Friday still sums to 1.00 (0.40/0.30/0.30). This matters because partitionCasesByShare() (workers/agent-runner.js L1203) allocates each batch its slice of the day total UP FRONT and does not redistribute a slice whose block never fires: had the pre-dawn blocks simply been left outside the new cron window, 50% of a Sun-Thu day's questions and 70% of a Friday's would have been silently DROPPED, not deferred. Retiming preserves the day's volume exactly; leaving them would have cut it in half.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.spread_not_bunched: The batches were re-spread across the window rather than packed into the earliest free slots (owner constraint). Sun-Thu batches now run 08:00, 09:30, 11:00, 12:00, 13:30, 15:00 — roughly 90-minute spacing, interleaved with the 11:30 tool-task window and 12:30 chore rotation, which did not move because both were already inside the window. Friday's three run 08:00, 09:00, 10:00, finishing 30 minutes before its 10:30 report block.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.block_order_is_load_bearing: runScheduledBlock() derives isFirstBlock from blocks[0].time and isLastBlock from blocks[last].time (agent-runner.js L1839-1840) — the first entry OPENS the day cycle and the last entry FINALIZES it. Each `blocks` array below is therefore kept sorted by time. A future edit that appends a block out of order, or that moves the earliest/latest time without reordering the array, will break day open/close rather than just misplace a block.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.saturday_unchanged: Saturday's two blocks were already at 08:00 — the new window's first tick — so they did not move and Saturday remains a zero-simulation-activity day.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.every_block_time_must_land_on_a_cron_tic: Ticks fire at :00 and :30 only, from 08:00 to 18:00 Israel inclusive. A block at any other minute, or outside that range, is simply never reached — runScheduledBlock() matches on an exact time string.

work_hours._corrected_2026_08_06: Was 08:00-16:00. Widened to match the office-hours cron window (08:00-18:00 Israel) so this file stops disagreeing with itself — owner decision 2026-08-06. Behaviour comes from the cron window plus the `blocks` times, which is exactly why the two were able to drift apart unnoticed in the first place.

overtime_window.note: Per-agent overtime eligibility comes from agents-config.json work_routine.overtime (e.g. agent_2 '30%_of_days', agent_5 'regular', agent_10 'daily'). Overtime cases are drawn from the same daily pool via extendSession(), not a separate pool.
overtime_window._relationship_to_work_hours_2026_08_06: This window now sits INSIDE work_hours rather than after it, and that is deliberate, not a leftover. Read it as: the office is OPEN 08:00-18:00, and 16:00-18:00 is the portion of that only overtime-eligible agents work. Before 2026-08-06 work_hours ended at 16:00 and this was the extension past closing; the span an agent could possibly work was 08:00-18:00 either way, so no agent's hours changed.

Weekly executive summary: the 10-section markdown, the per-agent CSV and the public excerpt, plus the product version bumps. SESSION 35, ITEM D (2026-08-29) -- THE SPLIT. This block used to run the template trio AND runMeeting('weekly') AND runReportPipeline() in ONE invocation. Measured in D1 block_admissions across its only two real runs: 53.25 and 48 weighted subrequests against a usable 47 -- the first EXCEEDED Cloudflare's 50-per-invocation platform limit outright. admitBlock() classified it 'oversize', which in this estate means it RUNS ANYWAY (a silently missing weekly report is a worse failure than a known overflow), so the overflow was a standing bet that the cheap part happened to run first. The ceiling was NOT raised. The work was split along its own seams instead: this tick keeps the template trio + product version bumps, 12:30 runs the meeting, 13:00 runs the reviewed report. Same three outputs, same order, produced in parts.

Weekly meeting -- runMeeting('weekly'). SPLIT OFF weekly_summary 2026-08-29 (SESSION 35, ITEM D). It is the expensive third: BLOCK_COST.meeting is 34 against a usable 47 and was measured live at 31 on a real tick, and it had been sharing one invocation with two other pieces of work of comparable size. Its own tick is its own invocation budget -- the same remedy closing_qa_review took on 2026-08-15 and owner_channel, spare_time and guide_review took on 2026-08-16.

Weekly written report -- runReportPipeline('weekly'), behind report_pipeline_enabled. SPLIT OFF weekly_summary 2026-08-29 (SESSION 35, ITEM D). It runs AFTER the meeting, exactly as it did inside the combined block, so the meeting's decisions are already filed when the fact pack is built. It recomputes agentRows and the pipeline summary rather than carrying them across ticks: the only carrier would be the KV day cycle, which is the very thing an overflowing tick was already failing to persist -- see workers/subrequest-budget.js's header.

Closing QA review — same wiring as full_day_schedule's 15:30 entry; Friday is a work day (short) so today's output still gets reviewed before the week closes. MOVED HERE FROM 12:00 on 2026-08-15 (OB-073), for the same reason as the weekday move: it had been grouped with weekly_summary, daily_standup, spare_time AND guide_review all at 12:00 -- the single most crowded tick in either schedule, immediately preceding finalizeScheduledDay(). Split across 12:00 (3 blocks) and 12:30 (2 blocks) instead of 5 at one tick. MOVED 12:30 -> 13:30 on 2026-08-29 (SESSION 35, ITEM D). It is the day's LAST block and blocks[last] finalizes the day (block_order_is_load_bearing above), so it moves to stay last once weekly_meeting took 12:30 and weekly_report took 13:00. Friday now closes at 13:30 instead of 12:30. Running the closing review AFTER the weekly package is complete is also the more correct order: it reviews more of the day than it used to.

saturday_schedule.label: REST DAY — genuinely zero-write since 2026-08-10. No case batches, no meetings, no model calls of any kind, and NO REPO WRITE. One idle block, which makes no model call and commits nothing.

_rest_day_2026_08_10.what: TWO Saturday writes were removed, not one. `guide_verify` moved to Friday 11:30, and the day-finalize repo commit is suppressed on an off day (workers/agent-runner.js finalizeScheduledDay(), guarded on the isOffDay argument it already received and had never used).
_rest_day_2026_08_10.why: docs/OFFICE-POLICY.md A13, owner-approved 2026-08-10 and confirmed by him the same day: 'Saturday is a rest day. Not for token saving — that is solved elsewhere — but as a safety floor: a day with no automated writing is a day accumulating error stops.' The policy is NEWER than this file's previous Saturday design, and where they disagreed the policy wins.
_rest_day_2026_08_10.the_second_write_was_not_in_the_brief_an: The known Saturday write was `guide_verify`. `finalizeScheduledDay()` was ALSO committing reports/daily/day-NNN-summary.md every Saturday, because the last block of the day triggers the finalize path and that path had no off-day branch on the commit — it took `isOffDay` as an argument and used it only to decide whether to run a milestone meeting. So Saturday had been writing a daily summary for every Saturday the cron has run. Found while implementing the first fix; recorded rather than quietly folded in, because 'we fixed the thing we were asked about' and 'Saturday is now zero-write' are different claims and only the second one is true now.
_rest_day_2026_08_10.what_still_happens_on_saturday_and_why_i: The idle block logs one `interactions` row per agent to D1 and finalize still advances the year/day counters in KV. Neither is automated authorship: A13's concern is a day of unattended WRITING accumulating unchecked, and a counter that must advance for Sunday to exist is not that. If the office ever stops advancing the day on Saturday, Sunday's cycle opens on a stale day number — which is a worse failure than the one A13 guards against.
_rest_day_2026_08_10.guide_verify_new_home: Friday 11:30 Israel — a free cron tick, after the Friday report/guide_draft at 10:30 and the owner_channel at 11:00, and before the 12:00 weekly close. The pass is still WEEKLY and still one run; only the day moved.

daily_ai_experience_report.who: every agent who asked at least one question today
daily_ai_experience_report.what: a short, casual fileStatusReport()-style note (1-2 paragraphs) on today's experience asking Claude/Gemini real questions: what worked, what didn't, tone matches the agent's personality.
daily_ai_experience_report.permission_level: private (staff/agents + owner) per CLAUDE.md report tiering — these are internal mood/experience notes, not business-facing.

capability_gap_reporting._meta: SUPERSEDED the old 'model_education_case_study' sub-block 2026-07-18 (Q&A-engine rebuild). No longer batched at end of day from 'the worst N interactions' — each ask-and-evaluate call (agents/agent-base.js askAssignedProject()) decides in real time via workers/gap-reports.js detectCapabilityGap() + the agent's own escalation_threshold (config/agents-config.json, see Step 3 persona differentiation).
capability_gap_reporting.trigger: HARD gaps (no Notebook-X answer at all, or the Claude request itself failed) always flag, any persona. SOFT candidates (a real but weak answer, quality < 0.5) only flag if quality is also below THIS agent's escalation_threshold — sensitive personas (QA, Lead QA) flag more of these than tolerant ones (Standard, Trainee).
capability_gap_reporting.what: a short (2-4 line) HEBREW internal office note, in the flagging agent's own voice via queryGeminiDirect() (Gemini composes the Hebrew — the Groq-routed path is English-only persona flavor): what's missing/wrong, where (topic/notebook), what it teaches. Framed as "the tool I work with isn't good enough here, flagging it for the tool to be fixed" — internal office logic, not a customer-facing incident.
capability_gap_reporting.routing: agent.fileGapReport() persists a `reports` row (type='gap_hebrew', project set). Once per day at this 'report' block, agent-runner.js's fileGapDigests() reads today's rows, groups by project, and commits ONE file per project with entries to reports/gaps/<project>/<date>.md. NEVER a GitHub Issue, for either project — an explicit requirement of this rebuild, unlike the old model_education_case_study which did open one.
capability_gap_reporting.permission_level: special (AI staff + owner) — internal, Hebrew, not business-facing.

_tool_task_window_retired_2026_08_17.what: The Sun-Thu 11:30 `tool_task_window` block was REMOVED from full_day_schedule.blocks on 2026-08-17 (OB-132). `maybeOpenAssetTask()` in agent-runner.js is NOT deleted and is still reachable — see `asset_task_window` under trigger types.
_tool_task_window_retired_2026_08_17.why: It fired every weekday, was admitted with `decision: run`, and returned `not_eligible` every time since simulation day 6. The cause was not a bug: `maybeOpenAssetTask()` refuses when `item.stage !== 'queued' || item.asset_task_issue_filed`, and ALL FOUR standing_project_ref items in reports/asset-pipeline/board.json — qa-knowledge-base, archives-app, designer-tooling-suite, architect-org-products — carry `asset_task_issue_filed: true`, stamped on simulation days 5, 6, 7 and 8. There are exactly four standing projects across the five rotation days (Thursday reuses archives-app), each files its Issue ONCE, and nothing ever un-files the flag. The block did its whole job by day 8 and has been firing 5x a week ever since with nothing it could possibly do.
_tool_task_window_retired_2026_08_17.why_retired_rather_than_fixed: Its queue can only refill when a HUMAN executes the tool work in the real external tool (NotebookLM/Stitch/Base44/Google AI Studio have no unattended API — that is the premise of the whole asset pipeline, see ai-tools.json) and a session then edits board.json. All four items are still `stage: queued` from day 1, so that has never once happened. A queue whose only filler is an off-schedule human act does not earn a place on a 5-day-a-week schedule. This is the opposite call from admin_desk above, deliberately: those four queues refill on their own (a probation counter ticks per case answer, incidents accrue, reviews come owed as builds finish), so an empty desk there is a queue that will fill.
_tool_task_window_retired_2026_08_17.not_the_third_state: The rejected option was to leave it scheduled and make it silent. A block that fires, records success and does nothing is the shape this project has named repeatedly (OB-131, OB-132, KFM). Making it quiet would have removed the evidence without removing the block.
_tool_task_window_retired_2026_08_17.how_to_run_it_when_there_is_real_work: POST /api/agents/trigger {"type":"asset_task_window","dayOfWeek":1} — the capability is intact, it is just no longer on a timer. The day a human returns an asset and a session queues a new board item, that trigger files its Issue.

admin_desk_program.description: The admin tier's scheduled draw from real queues. ADDED 2026-08-17. Sun-Thu 10:00 Israel only — NOT Friday: every Friday tick from 08:00 to 12:30 already carries a block, and blocks[last] finalizes the day (see block_order_is_load_bearing above), so a Friday entry would either share a crowded tick or move the day's close. admin_desk_program.why_it_exists: On 2026-08-11 `in_case_rotation: false` correctly removed agents 5-9 and 11 from the daily Q&A case rotation — admins were solving support cases while their real roles went unenforced. NOTHING REPLACED IT. Measured against live D1 on 2026-08-17: none of those six agents had a `reports` row later than 2026-08-11 13:00. Six days, half the office, zero output.
admin_desk_program.the_rule: Each desk reads a queue that exists for its own reasons and that something else fills. AN EMPTY QUEUE PRODUCES NOTHING — no file, no reports row, no D1 write, no model call, and no 'nothing to do' artifact either. A scheduled block that records success while doing nothing is worse than an unscheduled one, because it looks like activity (KFM, and the shape of OB-131/OB-132).

desks.deliverable_review: Agents 5,6,7,8,9,11,12,13 — deliverables at IN-REVIEW whose `owed_by` names them, read from campus/shared/lifecycle/IN-FLIGHT.md via the office snapshot. Capped at 2 per tick and the cap is REPORTED, never silent. A deliverable whose board task is NOT-READY or DONE is not carried and is skipped (OB-043's site build was reassigned to the owner). A review is refused, not fabricated, when the artifact itself cannot be read — a warehouse-located deliverable is not readable from the Worker.

build_chain_program.description: Sun-Thu 11:30 (repair) and 13:00 (architect_approval). Session 33, Item B. The two halves of Session 31's build chain, put on the tick. Both were built, both ran live, and NEITHER was schedulable -- not because nobody wrote the cron line, but because each takes {slug, agentId, findingText} as arguments and a tick has no arguments. The missing piece was somewhere for the chain to remember what it was in the middle of; that is D1 `build_chain` (workers/build-chain.js).
build_chain_program.the_queue_fills_itself: There is no source of blocking findings for a warehouse artifact -- the Worker holds no warehouse READ token, so the admin desk records every warehouse-located deliverable as unreadable and draws no review slot for it (session 30, item A). So the Architect's approval is BOTH the consumer and the producer of findings on this path: a `block` verdict's reasoning IS the next repair's finding. Session 31 proved that empirically, twice, with two correct blocks that each named a real defect. build_artifact -> AWAITING-APPROVAL -> (block) -> AWAITING-REPAIR -> (repaired) -> AWAITING-APPROVAL -> (approve+merge) -> MERGED. Bounded by admin-desk.js repairDecision(): the THIRD attempt at the same finding is refused and the row STALLS, surfaced once to the owner rather than spending the budget forever.

the_ceilings_and_where_they_come_from.repair: MAX_REPAIRS_PER_TICK = 1. A repair is one Cerebras build_artifact-lane call producing a COMPLETE file -- Session 31 measured that lane's real output at up to 371 lines and set its max_tokens from that measurement. Two per invocation would be two whole-file generations plus four GitHub commits against Cloudflare's 50-subrequest ceiling. It is also right for a non-budget reason: a repair addresses ONE named finding, and the next finding is not known until the Architect has seen the repaired file, so two per tick would mean the second repairing against a finding raised before the first landed.
the_ceilings_and_where_they_come_from.architect_approval: MAX_APPROVALS_PER_TICK = 1, and this is a MONEY ceiling as much as a subrequest one. Every approval is a direct Anthropic call on the component:'architect' sub-budget, which is $1.00/month -- the smallest of the three Claude sub-budgets. One per weekday is ~22 calls a month, which it carries; two is ~44, and the budget would run out silently mid-month, refusing every approval for the remainder while the repair loop kept queueing work for it.

build_chain_program.the_spend_guard_is_enforced_on_this_path: Checked INSIDE runArchitectApprovalCall() (workers/architect-spec.js): getClaudeBudgetStatus(env, {component:'architect'}) runs before callClaudeMessages() and returns a REFUSAL, not a degrade -- there is no fallback model for the Architect. It is not at any call site, so the supervised trigger and this scheduled block are guarded by one check in one place and a third caller added later cannot bypass it. scripts/verify-build-chain.js runs the real function against an over-budget D1 double with globalThis.fetch as a tripwire, so the guard has been WATCHED refusing something. KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than discovered: with no D1 binding getClaudeBudgetStatus() treats spend as $0 and does NOT refuse ('degrades open', its own words). The guard depends on D1 being readable.
build_chain_program.the_entry_point_is_still_supervised: `build_artifact` -- the block that CREATES an AWAITING-APPROVAL row -- is NOT on this schedule. Session 31 gave it exactly one supervised live run, and CLAUDE.md's graduated-rollout rule is not satisfied by one. Putting the office's first autonomous code-artifact writer on a timer is a separate owner decision and Session 33 did not take it. CONSEQUENCE, said here rather than discovered: once the seeded queue drains, these two blocks have no autonomous source of work and will correctly report an empty queue -- which the daily obligation check (Item A) will then record as a day that produced nothing.
build_chain_program.not_on_friday: Same reason admin_desk_program gives: every Friday tick from 08:00 to 12:30 already carries a block, and blocks[last] finalizes the day (block_order_is_load_bearing), so a Friday entry would either share a crowded invocation or displace the finalize.

spare_time_program.description: Fires whenever an agent has no more assigned cases for the day and no meeting to attend. Two outcomes, chosen per agent:

coworker_interaction.what: one short Gemini call generating a brief in-character exchange between this agent and a related agent (relationships.json partnerships/rivalries preferred), logged as an `interactions` row (type='coworker_chat'). Costs exactly 1 Gemini call.

idle.what: agent goes idle: state is saved as-is, an `interactions` row (type='idle', no query/response) is logged for the daily summary, and ZERO Gemini/Claude calls are made. This is the default and MUST be the only path on Saturdays (force_idle).
idle.token_savings: this is the primary token-discipline lever for spare time, per Launch Decisions.

qa_instruments_program.description: Friday 09:30. Runs the office's two cross-agent QA instruments and files one markdown finding into back-office. Added 2026-08-15 to close audit finding #8 / KFM-10: cross-embodiment comparison and review-the-reviewers were both built, both marked capability-SUPPLIED, and both reachable only via /api/agents/trigger — no scheduled block referenced either, so neither had ever run on its own. The office's entire quality argument rests on cross-agent review, and the two instruments that perform it had no autonomous caller.
qa_instruments_program.gate: improvement_loop_enabled. NO SWITCH OF ITS OWN, deliberately: the defect being closed here is a built capability with no autonomous caller, and shipping it behind a fresh OFF switch would reproduce that defect on the very feature meant to fix it. Riding improvement_loop_enabled is an honest dependency, not a borrowed one — the comparison reads exactly the rows workers/improvement-loop.js writes, and with the loop off there is nothing to compare.

qa_instruments_program.what_it_does_not_do: review-the-reviewers is VALIDATION, not a verdict. It never fills in a decision the CEO has not made — that would be the fabricated attribution OB-075 gated the same day.

guides_program.description: Owner-directed special task for the dormant Architect persona (agent 10) — see CLAUDE.md 'Guides'. Two model calls per guide: a writer persona (chosen by domain, workers/guide-engine.js pickWriterAgentId()) drafts via Gemini; the Architect reviews/finalizes via a DIRECT Anthropic API call (workers/claude-client.js, model claude-sonnet-5, tracked against its OWN $4.50/mo sub-budget — config/token-economy.json guides_claude_budget, workers/model-router.js component:'guides'). Stores the draft in D1 guide_pipeline (status='drafted'); does not commit anything itself.

guide_review.what: Self-healing: if today's draft is missing (missed tick, or Gemini paced out), generates it in the same tick before reviewing (one Gemini + one Claude call in one invocation — well within Cloudflare subrequest limits). The Architect reviews via Claude: APPROVE commits guides/<domain>/<slug>.md and appends any UNVERIFIED sections to guides/_verification-queue.md; REVISE sends fixes back to the writer for ONE revision round then re-reviews; REJECT (or a failed second review) commits the draft + rejection note to guides/_drafts/<slug>.md instead. Never escalates to the owner — fire-and-forget, log and move on.

owner_channel_program.description: REQ-001's base — the owner↔office channel, built 2026-08-10 under owner supervision. THE BASE ONLY: the presentation layer, the visual page over the channel and its security review are the office's work and are on the delegation board. The split is a trust boundary, not a division of labour — an office that builds its own instruction channel builds the pipe that feeds it.
owner_channel_program.code: workers/owner-channel.js (parsers, the read record, the age ladder), workers/owner-notify.js (the GitHub-Issue hop and the weekly heartbeat), wired into prompts by workers/office-context.js and run by processOwnerChannelBlock() in workers/agent-runner.js.
owner_channel_program.kill_switch: SIM_KV simulation-state `owner_channel_enabled`. Absent or false — the SHIPPED CODE DEFAULT — makes this block a logged no-op: no receipt is written and no Issue is filed. Toggle without redeploy: POST /api/agents/trigger {"type":"owner_channel_toggle","enabled":true|false}. Read-back (no Issue, no model call): {"type":"owner_channel_status"}. Supervised single run with the gate bypassed — THIS FILES A REAL ISSUE: {"type":"owner_channel_block"}. NOTE per OB-040 that this sentence describes the code default and makes no claim about production.
owner_channel_program.what_the_block_does: Two acts, in order. (1) RECORDS WHAT WAS READ: every message in back-office channel/from-owner/ whose CONTENT the office has no receipt for gets one, in channel/from-office/READ-LOG.md and in D1 owner_channel_reads. The record is the deliverable — a folder of messages cannot tell an unread message from one read and ignored, and a dated row carrying the content SHA can. (2) NOTIFIES: open submissions plus any question that has climbed the age ladder go out as one GitHub Issue, and on Sunday one goes out even when there is nothing to say.
owner_channel_program.reading_is_continuous_the_BLOCK_is_not: Owner messages reach agent prompts through the office-context snapshot cache (30-minute TTL, refreshed by the meeting engine and the report renderers), NOT through this block. This block exists to RECORD and to NOTIFY. So a message the owner writes at 09:00 is in front of the office within half an hour; what waits for 16:00 is the receipt and the outbound notification.
owner_channel_program.the_one_day_lag_stated_rather_than_hidde: The Sun-Thu block runs at 16:00, BEFORE the 16:30 standup. A submission or question opened in that standup is therefore notified the NEXT day, up to ~24h later. Accepted deliberately: putting the block after the standup would make it the day's last block, which is the block that triggers the day finalize, and hanging the finalize on a single-purpose tick is a worse trade than a day of latency on a channel a human answers in days.
owner_channel_program.why_a_GitHub_Issue_does_not_contradict_t: The 2026-07-18 Q&A rebuild set a hard rule that capability-gap digests are NEVER a GitHub Issue, for either project. That rule is about GAP REPORTS — machine-generated findings produced at a rate that would turn the tracker into a log file. An owner-communication Issue is addressed to a PERSON, is rate-limited by the office's actual decisions, and exists because the owner already gets GitHub notifications on his phone (OB-023 criterion 1: he must not have to acquire a new habit). Different thing, owner-approved, and labelled `owner-channel` so the two can never be confused.
owner_channel_program.how_it_fails_loudly: OB-023 criterion 2. THE SENDER LEARNS: every attempt is recorded in D1 owner_notifications with its HTTP status, successes and failures alike, and a failure is surfaced in the daily report, in office-context's errors section (so it rides in EVERY agent prompt until it clears) and in the status trigger. THE RECEIVER LEARNS A MESSAGE WAS LOST: every notification carries a sequence number and names the previous one, so a gap is visible in the message that DID arrive. THE RECEIVER LEARNS NOTHING ARRIVED AT ALL: the Sunday heartbeat is sent even when there is nothing to report, which is the only mechanism that can answer the owner's own disqualifier — 'an option whose only failure signal is my eventually noticing nothing arrived is indistinguishable from a quiet week'. Once the channel always speaks, a quiet week still produces a message.
owner_channel_program.the_residual: If the Worker itself stops running, no heartbeat is sent and nothing here notices. That is OFFICE-POLICY A16's class of failure — 'he cannot catch a failure that stops him from running' — and its answer is an external check from a different machine. Wiring the heartbeat's absence into the midnight run is BOARDED, not built. A session that reads this program and concludes the channel cannot drop anything has read it wrong.

_blocks_retired_2026_08_29._session: SESSION 34, ITEM B — Claude Code, unsupervised, 2026-08-29.
_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.what_this_is: A RETIREMENT, NOT AN OMISSION. Nine `case_batch` blocks and five `guide_*` blocks were removed from the schedules above on 2026-08-29. NOTHING WAS DELETED FROM THE CODE: workers/qa-engine.js, workers/qa-topics.js, workers/gap-reports.js, workers/gemini-pacer.js, workers/guide-engine.js, workers/claude-client.js, every one of the block handlers in workers/agent-runner.js, and BOTH kill switches (`cases_enabled`, `guides_enabled`) are exactly where they were. Only the SCHEDULE ENTRIES are gone. The verbatim JSON of every removed block is preserved in `removed_blocks` below, so restoring one is a copy-paste and not a reconstruction.
_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.why: Both features were already switched OFF, and the schedule went on admitting them anyway — four to six blocks a day entering the invocation budget, taking their turn in the admission loop, and producing nothing. Measured in D1 `block_admissions`: EVERY `case_batch` from 2026-08-24 onward has `actual: 0` (the last non-zero was 2026-08-23, the day the switch was thrown), and every `guide_*` run from 2026-08-21 onward has `actual: 0`. Two of them were also DEFERRED on 2026-08-28 — the office was spending admission decisions to refuse blocks that would have done nothing had they been admitted.

the_two_switches_this_follows.cases_enabled: Case work (the Q&A engine) was RETIRED BY THE OWNER on 2026-08-23 — see back-office-AI-agents/docs/decisions/RETIRED-CAPABILITIES.md R-001, enforced the same day by SESSION 10, and `cases_enabled` reads back FALSE from live SIM_KV. R-001 records in its own text that the six weekday `case_batch` blocks were deliberately LEFT IN PLACE at the time, because no switch existed yet. The switch exists now. This is the later, dated note that removes them.
the_two_switches_this_follows.guides_enabled: The guides pipeline has read FALSE in live SIM_KV since 2026-08-20. Its kill switch is untouched and still works in both directions.

_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.how_to_restore: Paste the block back into the `blocks` array of the named schedule, in `time` order, AND flip the matching switch back on (`POST /api/agents/trigger {"type":"cases_toggle"|"guides_toggle","enabled":true}`). BOTH halves are required and neither works alone: a schedule entry with the switch off is precisely what this retirement removed, and a switch with no schedule entry has nothing to fire it. For `case_batch` specifically, restore ALL of a schedule's entries together — `case_share` is a proportion of the day's total and the values below sum to exactly 1.0 per schedule, so restoring a subset silently drops that fraction of the day's questions with no error.

block_counts.saturday_schedule: 1 -> 1 (unchanged — the rest day carries one force_idle spare_time block and nothing else)

_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.a_side_effect_worth_knowing: With no `case_batch` left on any schedule, `casesDue` is now false on every tick. That changes two things in workers/subrequest-budget.js, both in the right direction and neither by editing a limit: the tail reserve drops from TICK_TAIL_RESERVE (6) to TICK_TAIL_RESERVE_NO_CASES (3), and the 60% case floor becomes 0. Usable budget per tick therefore goes from 44 (of which only 18 was available to non-case work) to 47, all of it. That is the real budget this item frees — not the estimates the dead blocks were claiming, which cost nothing because the blocks spent nothing.
_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.what_this_did_NOT_fix: The 2026-08-28 `architect_liaison` deferral is NOT solved by this item, and that was CHECKED rather than assumed. That block shares the Friday 11:00 tick with `owner_channel`, and neither is removed here; it was starved by a wrong ESTIMATE (14 declared against a measured 2), which is Session 34 Item A. Removing dead blocks freed schedule slots and ticks; it freed almost no measured subrequests, because every block removed was already spending zero. Recorded plainly so a future reader does not credit this item with Item A's fix.
_blocks_retired_2026_08_29.also_checked_and_deliberately_left: D1 `block_admissions` was queried for every block whose `actual` has been 0 on every run in the last fourteen days. The four types removed here are the COMPLETE list; no other block came back. `architect_liaison` has a single 0 row and it is the 2026-08-28 `defer` — a block that never ran, not a block that ran and did nothing — so it was left alone. A block producing zero may be broken rather than retired, and removing it would hide that.
